children: Shares in Bunzl rose after the company launched a new 500 million-pound ($677.4 million) share buyback plan and lifted its full-year guidance after a strong first-half performance.
In morning trading, London-listed shares were up 2.2% at 28.54 pounds. Year to date, shares have risen by over 37%.

The U.K. distribution and services group said Tuesday that it now expects its 2026 operating margin to be broadly flat versus last year's, instead of slightly down on-year previously. Last year, the company's operating margin was 7.6%.
It also projects modest adjusted operating profit growth on-year and still anticipates modest underlying revenue growth.

For the first-half, pretax profit rose to 290.4 million pounds from 250.1 million pounds for the same period a year earlier, while adjusted operating profit grew to 440.6 million pounds from 404.5 million pounds.

Revenue increased to 5.93 billion pounds from 5.76 billion pounds. On an underlying basis, revenue in North America, and the U.K. and Ireland grew 4.6% and 1.3%, respectively. Meanwhile, underlying revenue for Continental Europe was up 2.1%.

"Bunzl regained a degree of commercial agility to drive some meaningful new business wins by fourth quarter which teed up 2026 for a better revenue performance," RBC Capital Markets analysts Karl Green and Andrew Brooke wrote in a note to clients.
The company said that the buyback program would be completed over the next 12 months, in line with its policy to distribute excess cash while keeping headroom for acquisitions.
The board declared an interim dividend of 20.8 pence a share, up from 20.2 pence a share a year earlier.
